summary: IDS feed s065_single is otherwise healthy (no drops, truncation, overload, duplicates, or one-way traffic) but 68.9% of bytes are encrypted, exceeding the IDS tolerance of 60%, reducing payload visibility and detection coverage.

findings.root_cause: Majority of traffic is TLS/encrypted (68.9% vs 60% threshold). Packet broker is forwarding encrypted sessions directly to the IDS without decryption or selective bypass, so the IDS sees only ciphertext.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs full payload for signature and anomaly detection; encrypted payloads are opaque, so exploits, malware and C2 inside TLS go undetected and IDS cycles are wasted on undecryptable flows.

recommended_fix.why: IDS cannot inspect encrypted payloads natively; add SSL visibility/decryption upstream of the packet broker or filter/bypass trusted encrypted categories to bring encrypted share below 60% and restore inspection efficacy.
